Neural networks have become the standard for tabular data analysis, yet they often struggle with interpretability and require extensive hyperparameter tuning. This paper introduces SAINT, a new architecture designed to address these limitations by integrating row attention mechanisms with contrastive pre-training. SAINT's row attention module enhances interpretability by assigning weights to individual rows, while its contrastive pre-training strategy improves generalization by learning representations from unlabeled data. Empirical results demonstrate that SAINT surpasses current state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmarks, achieving superior performance with fewer hyperparameters.

This study examines the transfer learning behavior of radio frequency (RF) machine learning models by utilizing synthetic data. We demonstrate that the efficacy of transferring knowledge from a source to a target domain is contingent upon the degree of similarity between their respective data distributions. Furthermore, we introduce a novel metric designed to quantify the similarity between source and target domains, which serves as a reliable predictor of transfer learning performance.

The center vortex model offers a compelling framework for understanding the confinement mechanism in quantum chromodynamics (QCD). However, the model encounters a significant challenge known as the Gribov problem, which arises from the non-uniqueness of the gauge-fixing procedure. This issue is particularly acute in the center vortex model, where the gauge-fixing condition is applied to the center-projected link variables. This paper introduces a novel approach to resolving the Gribov problem by incorporating center regions into the model. We demonstrate that this method successfully eliminates the Gribov problem and yields a consistent, well-defined center vortex model.

This study examines the annihilation of dark matter by analyzing the luminosity function of low surface brightness galaxies (LSBGs) from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3. We employ a semi-analytical model to forecast the galaxy luminosity function, incorporating the impact of dark matter annihilation on the intergalactic medium. Our results indicate that the observed luminosity function of LSBGs is consistent with the standard $\Lambda$CDM model, provided that the annihilation cross-section remains below $10^{-26} \text{ cm}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$.

Locating concepts within software systems is a critical task for developers, yet existing tools often struggle to identify the correct code elements when users provide imprecise or ambiguous search queries. To address this, we introduce QUICKAR, a novel system that leverages crowdsourced knowledge to automatically reformulate user queries. QUICKAR operates by first gathering a set of candidate terms from a crowd-sourced repository and then utilizing a machine learning model to rank these candidates based on their relevance to the original search. We evaluated QUICKAR using a dataset comprising 1,000 queries and 10,000 candidate terms, demonstrating that the system significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in query reformulation.

This study introduces a novel preconditioning strategy for the linear systems arising from the discretized multi-compartmental Darcy equations. The approach employs a block-diagonal preconditioner that incorporates a diagonal scaling matrix, ensuring robustness against variations in the permeability tensor. Numerical experiments confirm that the resulting preconditioned conjugate gradient method maintains a consistent number of iterations regardless of changes in the permeability tensor.

Dialogue summarization involves condensing lengthy conversations into concise, informative abstracts. While current state-of-the-art methods rely on extensive training data, this paper introduces a zero-shot abstractive summarization approach that leverages discourse relations to restructure dialogues. By utilizing discourse relations to identify the primary topic and key arguments, the model generates summaries without requiring any task-specific training data. Experiments on the MultiWOZ dataset demonstrate that this method achieves performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art models.

The accurate prediction of cross-section Doppler broadening is essential for the design and operation of nuclear reactors. This study introduces a new approach that employs a deep neural network (DNN) to model the relationship between cross-sections and temperature. The DNN is trained on data from the ENDF/B-VIII.0 library, which includes cross-sections for 100 isotopes across 10,000 temperature points. To ensure the model learns physically consistent representations, the training process incorporates a physics-informed loss function. This function integrates the cross-section's temperature derivative, the cross-section itself, and the cross-section's second derivative with respect to temperature. The resulting model demonstrates high accuracy, with a mean absolute percentage error of 1.1% for the 100 isotopes. Furthermore, the model's performance is validated against the JEFF-3.3 library, confirming its ability to generalize to data from different sources.

This paper introduces the concept of $n$-pre-Lie algebras, which serve as a non-associative extension of $n$-Lie algebras. We establish that the dendrification of an $n$-pre-Lie algebra yields a structure isomorphic to an $n$-ary dendriform algebra. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the dendrification of an $n$-ary dendriform algebra corresponds to a specific instance of the dendrification of an $n$-ary pre-Lie algebra.

This study examines a cell-free massive MIMO network where users are categorized into two distinct groups: those requiring high-quality service (HQS) and those needing low-quality service (LQS). The primary objective is to maximize the sum rate of the LQS group while ensuring that the minimum achievable rate of the HQS group meets a predefined threshold. The analysis assumes that the base station employs a maximum ratio transmission (MRT) scheme, while each access point utilizes a zero-forcing (ZF) beamforming strategy. The resulting optimization problem is non-convex; however, it is transformed into a convex form by applying a change of variables. The paper further investigates the impact of the number of access points and base station antennas on the system's performance.
This paper examines the uniform convergence of translation operators within the context of the Sobolev space $W^{1,p}([0,1])$.

The study of disordered materials under shear is essential for understanding the rheology of complex fluids, yet the connection between microscopic structure and macroscopic flow remains elusive. This work examines the link between structure and flow in a two-dimensional model of athermal, repulsive disks. We demonstrate that the system's memory of its initial state is encoded in its structure, specifically through the spatial distribution of local packing density. This structural memory is quantified by the local packing density field's correlation length, which is found to be proportional to the system's relaxation time. Furthermore, we show that the system's relaxation time is proportional to the inverse of the shear rate, a relationship that holds across various initial conditions and shear rates. These findings suggest that the system's structure, memory, and flow are interconnected, with the system's memory of its initial state being encoded in its structure.

Object detection is a core component of computer vision, with deep learning methods achieving remarkable success in this field. However, these methods often struggle with catastrophic forgetting when trained on non-stationary data streams, a phenomenon known as continual learning. This paper reviews the current state of continual object detection, covering its definitions, strategies, and challenges. We begin by defining continual object detection and outlining its primary applications. Next, we examine the specific challenges inherent to this task, followed by a review of existing continual learning strategies. Finally, we conclude with a discussion of open research questions and potential future directions.

This study examines the medium-modified splitting function for the $g\to c\bar{c}$ process within the BDMPS-Z framework. We derive the medium-modified splitting function for the $g\to c\bar{c}$ process using the BDMPS-Z formalism.

Domain generalization (DG) aims to enhance model performance on unseen target domains by leveraging training data from multiple source domains. While recent DG methods have achieved promising results, they often fail to generalize effectively to out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. This limitation stems from the fact that these methods typically focus on aligning source domain distributions without adequately addressing the domain shift between sources and the target domain. To address this, we introduce a novel DG framework that integrates explainability to better capture the domain shift. Our approach employs a two-stage process: first, it utilizes an explainability-based domain adaptation strategy to align source and target domains by identifying and aligning the most discriminative features; second, it applies a domain-invariant feature learning technique to ensure robustness against domain shifts. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

The Internet's current architecture is increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks, which are becoming more frequent and sophisticated. This paper introduces a new framework designed to enhance security, knowledge sharing, and collaboration among agents within the Internet infrastructure. This framework leverages blockchain technology to establish a decentralized, immutable ledger for recording agent interactions. By utilizing this ledger, agents can verify the authenticity of transactions and build trust in one another. Furthermore, the system employs a consensus mechanism to ensure agreement on the ledger's state, thereby guaranteeing data integrity and consistency across the network.

$\alpha$-attractor models are a class of inflationary theories that are highly favored by observational data. This work examines the predictions of these models, specifically focusing on the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$) and the scalar spectral index ($n_s$). We demonstrate that the $n_s$-$r$ trajectories for $\alpha$-attractor models are nearly indistinguishable from those of the corresponding $\alpha$-inflation models. Furthermore, we analyze the parameter space of $\alpha$-attractor models and identify the most viable candidates. Our findings indicate that the $\alpha$-attractor model with a linear potential ($\alpha$-attractor) is the most favored, as it aligns best with current observational constraints.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming numerous sectors, including healthcare, finance, and transportation. However, the growing complexity of AI models and the escalating volume of data have created a critical need for efficient, high-performance computing resources. This paper examines the optimization of end-to-end AI pipelines on Intel Xeon processors, covering the full spectrum from data preprocessing to model inference. We outline specific strategies for optimizing each stage, such as leveraging parallel processing, memory hierarchy, and hardware accelerators. Furthermore, we present empirical findings from experiments conducted on real-world datasets, demonstrating the tangible performance gains achieved through these optimization techniques.

This study examines the relationship between the Bayes factor, the frequentist equivalence test, and the region of practical equivalence (ROPE) within the context of the highest density interval (HDI). We demonstrate that the Bayes factor can be approximated with high precision by calculating the area under the curve of the posterior distribution within the ROPE. Furthermore, we show that the frequentist equivalence test can be derived from the ROPE by applying a specific transformation to its boundaries. These findings suggest that the three methods are fundamentally linked, with the ROPE serving as the common underlying structure.

This paper introduces a novel vector quantized semantic communication framework designed to enhance the efficiency of semantic transmission. The system operates by encoding the semantic meaning of the source message into a compact codebook, which is then transmitted to the receiver. Upon reception, the codebook is decoded to reconstruct the original semantic information. The study evaluates the system's performance through the mean squared error (MSE) between the source and reconstructed messages, alongside the bit rate required for the codebook. The proposed vector quantization method is benchmarked against a baseline approach utilizing a fixed-length codebook. The results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves superior performance, delivering lower MSE and reduced bit rates compared to the baseline.

Big Data Analytics (BDA) is a rapidly expanding field that has garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. While BDA encompasses a wide range of applications, it is fundamentally defined by the analysis of massive datasets. The primary objective of BDA is to extract valuable insights from these data, which can be achieved through various methods, including data mining, machine learning, and data analytics. However, the sheer volume of data often renders traditional analytical approaches ineffective. Consequently, there is a growing demand for BDA systems that are interactive, adaptive, and capable of delivering results. This paper presents a novel framework designed to address these requirements. The proposed framework is built upon a new architecture that integrates a data processing engine, a data management system, and a user interface. The data management system is responsible for storing and managing the data, while the data processing engine handles the analytical tasks. The user interface enables users to interact with the system and view the results. The framework is evaluated using a real-world dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in meeting the interactive, adaptive, and result-aware criteria.

This paper examines the relationship between doctrines, modalities, and comonads within a categorical framework. We demonstrate that a comonad on a category $\mathcal{C}$ corresponds to a specific type of modality within a logical structure defined by a functor from $\mathcal{C}$ to the category of posets. Furthermore, we establish that a comonad on $\mathcal{C}$ is equivalent to a modality in a logical structure governed by a functor from $\mathcal{C}$ to the category of preordered categories.

This study introduces a novel Bayesian nonparametric framework for the Grouped Network Autoregression (G-NAR) model, designed to handle time series data characterized by both network structures and groupings. The approach employs a graphical assistant to facilitate the selection of network lag orders and incorporates a Dirichlet process prior to estimate the autoregressive coefficients. The methodology is evaluated through simulation experiments and applied to analyze the dynamics of the COVID-19 pandemic.

This study introduces a novel framework for verifying scientific claims, which involves determining the truthfulness of a statement based on a provided set of evidence. The core challenge lies in the vastness of available evidence, which hinders the efficient retrieval of relevant information. To address this, we propose a two-stage approach: first, a retrieval stage that identifies a compact subset of pertinent evidence, followed by a verification stage that assesses the claim's validity using this condensed evidence. We evaluate our method on the SciFact dataset, demonstrating that it achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art models while significantly lowering computational costs.

Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) serves as a non-invasive imaging technique for visualizing the eye's internal structures. This study introduces a novel method for automatically segmenting the posterior eye segment from OCT scans. The proposed approach utilizes a U-Net architecture to identify the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and the internal limiting membrane (ILM). Following segmentation, the distance between these two layers is calculated to determine the central macular thickness (CMT). The method was validated using 100 OCT scans from the public dataset, achieving a Dice coefficient of 0.92 for the RPE and 0.89 for the ILM. Additionally, the CMT measurements yielded a mean value of 248.8 µm with a standard deviation of 24.1 µm.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework for estimating dynamic cognitive models, utilizing a neural network to approximate the posterior distribution of parameters. The approach is demonstrated through a case study of a two-alternative forced-choice task, where the neural network estimates the posterior of a drift-diffusion model's parameters. The results indicate that this method offers a viable alternative to traditional Markov chain Monte Carlo techniques for parameter estimation.
This paper introduces a novel explicit expansion method for determining Mersenne primes.

This paper introduces the inaugural treebank for Spoken Frisian-Dutch code-switching, which is annotated using the Universal Dependencies framework. The dataset comprises 1,000 sentences derived from a corpus of 100 hours of Frisian-Dutch code-switching audio. The text details the annotation process, outlines the specific annotation guidelines, and provides a preliminary analysis of the resulting data.

Photoevaporation is a primary mechanism for clearing protoplanetary discs, yet the specific impact of stellar mass on this process remains uncertain. This study utilizes the photoevaporation model developed by Kunitomo et al. (2014) to examine how stellar mass affects disc dispersal. We analyzed the evolution of discs around stars with masses ranging from 0.1 to 1.0 solar masses, assuming a constant mass-loss rate of $10^{-10} M_{\odot} \text{ yr}^{-1}$. Our results indicate that disc lifetimes are strongly dependent on stellar mass, with more massive stars dispersing their discs significantly faster than lower-mass stars. Specifically, discs around 0.1 solar mass stars persist for approximately 10 million years, whereas those around 1.0 solar mass stars dissipate in roughly 1 million years. We also evaluated the influence of disc mass and radius on dispersal timescales, finding that while disc mass has a minor effect, disc radius exerts a substantial impact. Consequently, we propose that the observed variation in disc lifetimes across different stellar masses is primarily driven by the differing radii of their discs.

This study introduces a novel class of explicit, high-order time integration techniques tailored for the isogeometric analysis of structural dynamics. These methods are derived by applying a generalized-$\alpha$ framework to the semi-discrete equations of motion, which are formulated using the isogeometric approach. The resulting schemes are characterized by their explicit nature, high-order accuracy, and the capacity to achieve arbitrary damping levels. Furthermore, the paper details the implementation of these methods within the commercial software Abaqus. Numerical experiments are conducted to validate the proposed algorithms and to assess their performance.

This study examines the dynamics of a Bose polaron within a one-dimensional double-well system, focusing on the decay of its energy residue. We demonstrate that this decay is driven by both interband and intra-band excitations. Specifically, the interband process involves the polaron transitioning from the lower to the upper band, while the intra-band process entails the polaron remaining in the lower band but creating an excitation within the same band. We derive analytical expressions for the decay rates of both mechanisms and determine the conditions under which each dominates. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of the interband excitation energy on the decay rate and the associated timescale.

This study addresses the challenge of planning logistics for disaster relief operations, specifically focusing on the dynamic allocation of resources to aid victims. The objective is to minimize the total expected cost, which encompasses both the expenses of transporting supplies and the penalties associated with unmet demand. The model incorporates a two-stage stochastic framework where the first stage involves pre-disaster decisions regarding the initial stockpiling of resources at various locations, while the second stage involves post-disaster actions to distribute these supplies to affected areas. The model accounts for the uncertainty of disaster impact, represented by a set of scenarios, and the uncertainty of demand, represented by a set of demand scenarios. Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are currently detecting the stochastic gravitational wave background (GWB) generated by supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs). While the majority of these binaries are expected to be circular, a small fraction may retain significant orbital eccentricity. This study introduces a novel, computationally efficient method for calculating the post-Newtonian (PN) waveform of eccentric SMBHBs, which is essential for analyzing PTA data. We benchmark this new approach against the standard method, which relies on numerical integration of the equations of motion. Our results indicate that the new method achieves accuracy comparable to the standard method at a fraction of the computational cost. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the new method can be extended to incorporate higher-order PN corrections, which are critical for modeling the GWB from eccentric SMBHBs.

This paper examines a global game framework where agents possess private signals regarding a fundamental state and must decide whether to act based on their own signals and the observed actions of others. We demonstrate that, under specific conditions, the equilibrium probability of an agent taking action is uniquely determined by the fundamental state. Furthermore, we establish that the equilibrium action probability is monotonically increasing with respect to the precision of private signals and the degree of interdependence among agents.

This study introduces a technique for characterizing high-loss dielectrics at terahertz frequencies using a single on-chip resonator. By analyzing the resonator's transmission spectrum, we determine the material's loss tangent and refractive index. The method's accuracy is validated through measurements of water, a substance with significant absorption in the terahertz range.

The COVID-19 pandemic has caused significant global disruption, resulting in millions of deaths and economic losses estimated at over $10 trillion. To mitigate these effects, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) have issued guidelines for social distancing, mask usage, and hygiene practices. However, widespread non-compliance with these measures has hindered their effectiveness. This paper introduces a novel framework designed to enhance adherence to such protocols by leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) and multi-source data processing. The proposed system, named AIRSENSE-TO-ACT, integrates data from various sources—including air quality sensors, cameras, and wearable devices—to monitor and analyze human behavior. By employing machine learning algorithms, the system identifies patterns of non-compliance and triggers real-time alerts to encourage corrective actions. The authors anticipate that this approach will significantly improve compliance rates, thereby reducing the transmission of the virus and alleviating the broader economic and social impacts of the pandemic.

This study introduces a multi-resolution framework for Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) designed to enhance the accuracy of fluid-structure interactions (FSI) in multi-phase flows. The approach employs a multi-resolution strategy to manage the disparity between the fine resolution required for fluid interfaces and the coarser resolution sufficient for solid boundaries. The proposed method is validated through two numerical experiments: a dam-break scenario involving a solid block and a two-dimensional sloshing case with a floating body. Results indicate that the multi-resolution SPH method achieves accuracy comparable to traditional SPH while significantly reducing computational costs.

This review examines the topological characteristics of nodal lines within momentum space, specifically focusing on their associated topological invariants and recent experimental realizations in photonic systems and others.
This document outlines the HL-LHC computing strategy for event generators, focusing on the software infrastructure required to support the anticipated increase in luminosity.
This paper examines the invariance property of partial means, which are defined as the average of a finite number of terms within a sequence.

We report the detection of a thick disk of molecular gas in the outer Milky Way, utilizing a sample of 120 CO(1-0) sources identified by the APEX telescope. These sources, located at Galactic radii between 10 and 16 kpc, were selected based on their high-velocity dispersion, which exceeds 10 km/s. The resulting velocity dispersion profile reveals a distinct thick disk component, characterized by a scale height of approximately 1.2 kpc and a velocity dispersion of roughly 15 km/s. This thick disk component accounts for about 20% of the total molecular gas mass in the outer Galaxy. The study also identifies a significant population of high-velocity dispersion sources within the thin disk, which are likely associated with star-forming regions.

This paper examines a closed economy featuring a single firm and a single worker, where the firm's production function is concave and differentiable, and the worker's utility function is also concave and differentiable. The analysis focuses on the strategic interaction between the firm and the worker, specifically regarding the firm's wage-setting behavior and the worker's labor supply decisions. The study derives the equilibrium wage and labor supply, and it demonstrates that the equilibrium wage is strictly positive.

This study examines the collective behavior of dense, disordered polar active matter, focusing on the interplay between active forces and steric hindrance. We demonstrate that the system's dynamics are governed by two competing mechanisms: the alignment of active forces, which promotes order, and steric hindrance, which drives disorder. We identify a phase diagram featuring a first-order transition from a disordered state to a dynamically ordered one, as well as a second-order transition from a dynamically ordered state to a disordered one. Furthermore, we observe that the system's dynamics are characterized by a non-equilibrium steady state, which exhibits a non-trivial distribution of particle velocities.

This study examines the semileptonic decays of doubly charmed baryons, specifically $\Xi_{cc}^{++}$, $\Omega_{cc}^{+}$, and $\Xi_{cc}^{+}$, utilizing the bag model. We calculate the relevant form factors and subsequently derive the decay widths and branching fractions for these processes.

This study introduces a new task focused on localizing an agent within a 3D environment using only dialogue. We present a dataset comprising 1,000 dialogues, each containing 10 turns, where the agent's position is described through natural language. We evaluate the performance of various models in identifying the agent's location from these descriptions. Our results indicate that while current models achieve only moderate success, the task holds significant potential for future advancements.

Vibration analysis is a widely used technique for diagnosing faults in rotating machinery. However, the effectiveness of this method relies heavily on the selection of appropriate frequency bands, a task that is often difficult for practitioners. This paper introduces a novel automatic frequency band selection method called the Band Relevance Factor (BRF). The BRF is derived from the correlation between the time-domain and frequency-domain representations of vibration signals. By applying BRF to a dataset of vibration signals from a bearing test rig, the study demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively identify relevant frequency bands.

This study presents muon-spin relaxation and rotation measurements on the noncentrosymmetric superconductors CaTSi3 (T = Ir, Pt) to investigate their superconducting ground states. The results indicate that both materials exhibit a single superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) of approximately 2.5 K. The muon-spin relaxation rate ($\lambda_\mu$) remains constant below $T_c$, suggesting that the superconducting gap is isotropic. Furthermore, the Knight shift ($K_\mu$) shows no significant change below $T_c$, implying that the spin susceptibility is unaffected by superconductivity. These findings suggest that the superconducting ground state in CaTSi3 is characterized by a fully gapped, spin-singlet pairing mechanism.

This study introduces a novel approach to solving high-dimensional optimal feedback control problems, specifically addressing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. The method employs a sparse grid framework to discretize the HJB equation, utilizing a characteristics-based scheme to resolve the resulting system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). The proposed algorithm is validated through numerical experiments on a linear-quadratic control problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling high-dimensional scenarios.

This study examines the classification of quantum measurements using qudits, which are quantum systems with a dimensionality greater than two. We introduce a novel quantum classifier that leverages the specific properties of qudits to achieve superior performance compared to existing methods. Our findings demonstrate that this classifier can effectively identify and distinguish between various types of quantum measurements.

This paper introduces a novel framework for modeling and controlling multi-energy dynamical systems, which are pivotal to the transition toward decarbonization. The proposed approach integrates the strengths of both data-driven and physics-based methodologies, utilizing a hybrid architecture that combines a data-driven component for capturing complex, non-linear dynamics with a physics-based component for representing energy flows. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this hybrid model through a case study involving a multi-energy system comprising a building, a heat pump, and a battery.

This study examines the application of machine learning to the two-dimensional percolation model. We employ a convolutional neural network to forecast the critical threshold for site percolation on a square lattice. Our findings indicate that the network can accurately predict the critical threshold for lattices with varying site probabilities, provided the training set includes a broad range of such probabilities.

This study introduces a rapid magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for measuring temperature distributions within a gas-solid fixed bed. The method utilizes a single-shot, gradient-echo-based MRI sequence to capture temperature data at a rate of 100 frames per second. The system's performance was validated using a water phantom, demonstrating a temperature sensitivity of 0.05 K and a spatial resolution of 0.5 mm. The technique was subsequently applied to a gas-solid fixed bed, where it successfully visualized temperature variations caused by the gas flow. The results indicate that the proposed rapid MRI approach is effective for monitoring temperature dynamics in gas-solid fixed beds.

We examine the superconducting phase diagram of UTe$_2$ by incorporating quenched randomness and thermal fluctuations. Our analysis reveals that the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) is highly sensitive to the strength of the random potential, which can be modulated by varying the concentration of Te atoms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the interplay between thermal fluctuations and quenched randomness can induce a reentrant superconducting phase. This phenomenon is characterized by a sequence of transitions: from a normal state to superconductivity, followed by a return to a normal state, and finally a re-emergence of superconductivity at lower temperatures.

Ultra-Wideband (UWB) technology is a promising candidate for next-generation wireless communication, offering high data rates and low latency. However, its performance is heavily dependent on the specific configuration of its physical layer (PHY) parameters. This paper introduces a novel deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework designed to automatically adjust UWB PHY settings in real-time. The proposed method utilizes a deep neural network to forecast the channel's bit error rate (BER) and employs a DRL agent to select optimal PHY configurations based on these predictions. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms traditional methods that rely on fixed PHY settings.

This study examines the k-Median clustering problem within the context of discrete Fréchet and Hausdorff distances. We demonstrate that the problem is NP-hard for both metrics and present a 2-approximation algorithm for the case of discrete Fréchet distance.

Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) represents a critical area of research with extensive applications in fields such as robotics, transportation, and healthcare. This paper introduces a novel MARL framework that leverages the primal-dual approach to address the underlying optimization challenges. By employing a double averaging technique, we derive a new algorithm that achieves a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ for the average regret, where $T$ denotes the number of iterations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed method attains an $O(1/T)$ convergence rate for the average duality gap.

This paper introduces a coalgebraic framework for the arithmetic $\mu$-calculi, a class of $\mu$-calculi that incorporate arithmetic operations. We demonstrate that the satisfiability problem for these calculi is decidable, with the complexity of the decision procedure depending on the specific arithmetic operations included.

This study introduces a low-rank tensor approach for reconstructing sparse initial states in partial differential equations (PDEs) using Isogeometric Analysis (IGA). The proposed method employs a low-rank tensor representation to model the initial state, which is then optimized by minimizing the discrepancy between the PDE's solution and observed data. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this technique through numerical experiments involving the Poisson equation and the heat equation.

Air quality monitoring is essential for safeguarding public health, yet the scarcity of ground sensors hinders the creation of high-resolution air quality maps. This study introduces a novel framework that leverages vehicle-based sensors to generate dense air quality maps. The approach utilizes a regression model to estimate pollutant concentrations at specific locations, followed by a facility location algorithm to determine optimal sensor placement. The resulting sensor network is designed to minimize the total estimation error across the entire area. The proposed method is evaluated using real-world data from the Los Angeles Air Quality Network, demonstrating its effectiveness in producing high-resolution air quality maps.
This paper investigates the Weil representation of a generalized linear group defined over a ring of truncated polynomials over a finite field, under a second-class involution.

Persuasive video generation (PVG) is a rapidly growing field that leverages artificial intelligence to create videos designed to influence human behavior. This survey examines the current state of PVG, highlighting its applications, challenges, and future directions. We begin by defining PVG and outlining its key components, including the target audience, persuasive goals, and the generated video content. Next, we explore the diverse applications of PVG, ranging from marketing and education to entertainment and political campaigning. We then review the core technologies underpinning PVG, such as natural language processing, computer vision, and generative models. Finally, we identify critical challenges and propose potential avenues for future research.

This study examines the dynamics of ions held in both quadrupole and octupole traps, focusing on the creation of squeezed coherent states of motion. We demonstrate that applying a specific time-dependent modulation to the trapping potential yields these states. Furthermore, we analyze the squeezing characteristics of the resulting states and evaluate their potential utility for quantum information processing.

Neuroscience models are frequently tuned to replicate experimental data, a process that often demands extensive computational resources. This study introduces a new method for automating the hyper-parameter tuning of such models, utilizing a Bayesian optimization framework. This approach is designed to minimize the number of required model evaluations, thereby reducing the computational load. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness by applying it to a neural network model of the visual cortex, which was trained to replicate the responses of neurons in the primary visual area (V1) of macaque monkeys.

Camouflaged object detection (COD) has recently gained significant attention, yet it remains limited to binary classification tasks. To address this, we introduce Camouflaged Instance Segmentation In-The-Wild (CIS-ITW), a novel task designed to segment camouflaged objects within natural environments. This task is particularly challenging because it requires distinguishing between camouflaged objects and their backgrounds, which are often visually similar. To support this research, we present CIS-ITW, a new dataset comprising 1,000 images annotated with instance segmentation masks. We also propose a new baseline method, CIS-Net, which integrates a COD module with an instance segmentation module to effectively handle the task. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CIS-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on the CIS-ITW dataset. Furthermore, we establish a benchmark suite for CIS-ITW to facilitate future research and development in this domain.

This study examines the impact of Lorentz violation on superconductivity, specifically analyzing how it alters the superconducting gap and the critical temperature. The analysis reveals that Lorentz violation can either enhance or diminish the superconducting gap, contingent upon the specific parameters involved.

The growing integration of AI into daily life has heightened the need for reliable and transparent systems. While AI models are often treated as "black boxes," their internal workings remain opaque, making it difficult to identify and address errors. This study introduces a crowdsourcing framework designed to detect and validate AI failures. We evaluated the approach using a commercial image recognition system, where participants were tasked with identifying and reporting specific failures. The results indicate that this method is both effective and efficient, successfully uncovering a diverse range of errors.

Object detection is a critical task in computer vision, yet it remains computationally demanding. This paper introduces a novel randomized decision routing (RDet) module designed to enhance detection efficiency. The module employs a randomized routing strategy to distribute feature maps across multiple branches, thereby reducing computational costs. Additionally, it incorporates a dynamic routing mechanism to adaptively adjust the number of branches based on the input image's complexity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 2.5% improvement in mAP over the baseline YOLOv4 model while reducing computational costs by 30%.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which involve making minimal, imperceptible perturbations to input data to cause significant prediction errors. To counter this, adversarial training has emerged as a leading defense strategy. However, this approach suffers from catastrophic overfitting, where models fail to generalize on clean data after training on adversarial examples. This paper introduces ZeroGrad, a novel method designed to mitigate such overfitting. ZeroGrad achieves this by employing a zero-gradient update rule for the loss function during adversarial training. The proposed method is straightforward to implement and requires no additional hyperparameters. Empirical results demonstrate that ZeroGrad effectively reduces catastrophic overfitting while maintaining strong robustness against adversarial attacks. Furthermore, we provide an analysis of the method's behavior and its impact on model generalization.

We demonstrate that the Thakurta metric, which is often cited as a solution to the Einstein equations for a black hole surrounded by a cosmological constant, is actually incorrect. This error stems from a flawed application of the Einstein equations, specifically the improper handling of the stress-energy tensor. Consequently, the Thakurta metric cannot be used to derive constraints on primordial black holes (PBHs) from LIGO-Virgo observations of binary black hole mergers.

This study examines the impact of persistent asset switches on a specific class of optimization algorithms inspired by hybrid control systems. We demonstrate that the resulting closed-loop system is globally asymptotically stable, provided the Lyapunov function's decrease rate exceeds the rate at which the Lyapunov function's value increases due to asset switches.

Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables the execution of computations on encrypted data, a capability that is currently hindered by significant performance limitations. While bootstrappable FHE offers a solution to these issues, it remains impractical for widespread use due to its high computational demands. This paper introduces BTS, a novel bootstrapping architecture designed to enhance the efficiency of FHE operations. BTS achieves this by integrating a specialized bootstrapping accelerator with a streamlined FHE framework. The accelerator employs a hybrid approach that combines the bootstrapping process with the relinearization step, thereby reducing the number of required homomorphic multiplications. Additionally, it utilizes a hybrid key-switching strategy to minimize the size of the resulting ciphertexts. Experimental results indicate that BTS achieves a 1.5x to 2.5x speedup over existing bootstrapping methods, while also decreasing the ciphertext size by 1.5x to 3.5x.

We introduce a solvable random matrix ensemble characterized by a logarithmic confining potential, which is defined by a specific partition function. This partition function is expressed as a Fredholm determinant involving a kernel that can be computed explicitly. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding eigenvalue density and demonstrate that it aligns with the predictions of the large $N$ limit of the two-dimensional Yang-Mills theory.

This study experimentally examines quantum correlations within a two-qutrit spin system, utilizing a pair of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. We evaluate both quantum discord and entanglement, revealing that while entanglement is absent, quantum discord persists. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the quantum discord in this system is robust against magnetic field variations.

This paper presents a new derivation of Bell's theorem that relies on locality rather than factorizability. This approach is more intuitive and easier to grasp than the standard factorizability-based version. It also offers a fresh perspective on the debate between local hidden variable theories and quantum mechanics, specifically regarding the nature of non-locality.

We introduce StyleGAN-V, a novel video generation framework that delivers high-quality, continuous video synthesis while maintaining the computational efficiency and architectural simplicity of StyleGAN2. By extending the concept of StyleGAN2's latent space to a continuous domain, we enable the generation of videos of arbitrary length. Our approach employs a dual-structure architecture: a generator that produces frames and a separate module that generates the latent codes for those frames. This design allows for the creation of videos of any desired duration. Furthermore, we propose a novel training strategy that leverages the generator's ability to produce frames of variable lengths, thereby enhancing the model's capacity to learn temporal dynamics. Empirical results demonstrate that StyleGAN-V achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple video generation benchmarks, including the ability to generate videos of any length.

We demonstrate that the degree of the map $\eta_{\mathcal{F}}$ is strictly less than that of $\eta_{\mathcal{E}}$ for any two elliptic curves $\mathcal{E}$ and $\mathcal{F}$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, provided that $\mathcal{F}$ possesses a rational 2-torsion point.

Thermoluminescence dosimetry (TLD) is a technique used to measure radiation exposure, particularly in nuclear medicine. This method involves heating a material that has absorbed radiation to release stored energy as light, with the intensity of this light correlating to the radiation dose received. However, the light emission rate varies based on the time elapsed since exposure, a factor known as the "glow curve." This study introduces a deep learning approach to estimate the exposure date from these glow curves. The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to analyze the glow curve data. The model was trained on a dataset comprising 1,000 glow curves from TLDs exposed to radiation at different times. The results demonstrate that the CNN can accurately estimate the exposure date with a mean absolute error of less than 10%. This approach offers a promising alternative to traditional methods for estimating exposure dates in TLD, potentially enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of radiation dose measurements in nuclear medicine.

This paper investigates the existence of solutions for a specific class of singular elliptic equations defined on complete Riemannian manifolds. The study employs the direct method of calculus of variations, utilizing the framework of variable exponent Sobolev-Orlicz spaces.

This study introduces a novel CBCT simulator designed to model the imaging characteristics of both kilovoltage (kV) and megavoltage (MV) systems. The simulator's performance was evaluated using a phantom containing a 10 cm diameter insert with a 1 cm thick central region, scanned via a kV CBCT system. The resulting simulated images were compared against actual experimental data. Additionally, the simulator was employed to forecast the impact of various beam hardening correction techniques on image quality. The findings indicate that the simulator effectively replicates the imaging properties of kV CBCT systems and can accurately predict the benefits of beam hardening correction.

LIME is a popular method for explaining predictions made by machine learning models. It operates by training a simple, interpretable model on a small set of synthetic data points generated by perturbing the original input. However, LIME's explanations can be unstable, as minor variations in the perturbed data may lead to significantly different results. To address this, we introduce S-LIME, a new approach that stabilizes LIME by employing a weighted ensemble of multiple LIME instances. We evaluate S-LIME across various models and datasets, demonstrating that it produces more consistent explanations than standard LIME.

This paper introduces a Bayesian framework designed to rectify classification errors by incorporating explanation feedback. The method employs a generative model to estimate the posterior distribution of class labels, conditioned on both the original input and the provided explanation. The model's parameters are learned from a dataset containing inputs paired with their corresponding explanations and ground-truth labels. The approach is evaluated on two tasks: classifying images of handwritten digits and categorizing images of animals.

The study presents a comprehensive analysis of the crystal-field excitations in TbInO$_3$, a triangular-lattice system that serves as a potential spin-liquid candidate. Utilizing a combination of polarized and unpolarized polarized neutron scattering, researchers identified the crystal-field levels of the Tb$^{3+}$ ions and determined that the ground state is a doublet. Furthermore, the study detected two distinct vibronic modes at 1.2 and 1.6 meV, which are attributed to the coupling between Tb$^{3+}$ ions and the surrounding oxygen atoms. These findings offer valuable insights into the magnetic and electronic characteristics of TbInO$_3$ and related materials.

This paper examines the power-of-mean curvature flow, defined as $H^{\alpha} = \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \kappa$, where $H$ represents the mean curvature, $\kappa$ the mean curvature power, and $\alpha$ a real parameter. We demonstrate that for any $\alpha > -1$, the flow preserves convexity. Furthermore, we establish that the flow is strictly parabolic when $\alpha > 0$ and non-degenerate when $\alpha > -1$.

This limitation hinders the network's ability to capture global dependencies, a capability that Fourier-based convolutions can provide. This paper introduces a new architecture, the Frequency Convolutional Network (FCN), which integrates Fourier-based convolutions into CNNs to enhance global feature extraction. This paper introduces DeepCluE, a novel framework designed to enhance image clustering by leveraging multi-layer ensembles within deep neural networks. The approach integrates two key components: a multi-layer ensemble strategy that aggregates predictions from various layers of a pre-trained network, and a clustering module that refines these predictions by generating cluster centroids and updating them iteratively. The method is evaluated on the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper introduces a framework designed to identify institutional risks by leveraging knowledge graphs and automated news profiling. The system integrates data from multiple sources, including financial reports, news articles, and social media, to construct a comprehensive knowledge graph. This graph is then analyzed using natural language processing and machine learning techniques to detect potential risks. The study evaluates the framework's performance on a dataset of institutional risks and demonstrates its ability to identify risks with high precision and recall.

This paper introduces a novel classification approach grounded in Topological Data Analysis (TDA). The method begins by computing persistent homology for each data sample, utilizing the resulting persistence diagram as a feature representation. Subsequently, a classifier is trained on these diagrammatic features to categorize the samples. The study evaluates the method's performance across multiple datasets, including both synthetic and real-world examples, and compares its results with those of other established techniques.

Contrasimilarity, a concept introduced by the author in 2019, is defined as a specific type of similarity between two games. This paper presents a game-theoretic characterization of contrasimilarity, demonstrating that two games are contrasimilar if and only if they are equivalent under a particular game transformation.
We present a representation of the string 2-group as a functor from the 2-groupoid of string 2-bundles to the 2-groupoid of gerbes.

This study examines the generation of ion-acoustic rogue waves within a double pair plasma environment, where both ions and electrons follow a non-extensive distribution. By employing the reductive perturbation technique, we derive the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to analyze the rogue wave characteristics. The findings indicate that the amplitude of these ion-acoustic rogue waves is significantly influenced by the non-extensive parameter, the density ratio of ions to electrons, and the temperature ratio of electrons to ions.

The parametric decay instability (PDI) of Alfvén waves is a critical mechanism for energy transfer in magnetized plasmas, yet its experimental verification remains elusive. This study presents a hybrid simulation of the PDI, modeling the interaction between a high-frequency Alfvén wave and low-frequency daughter waves within a laboratory-scale plasma. The simulation incorporates a realistic ion distribution function and accounts for the finite Larmor radius of ions. Results indicate that the PDI is triggered by the Alfvén wave's finite parallel wavenumber, with the growth rate increasing as this wavenumber rises. Furthermore, the PDI growth rate is found to be independent of the initial Alfvén wave amplitude.

This study examines the gravitational stability of filamentary molecular clouds, accounting for the effects of ambipolar diffusion. We derive the dispersion relation for a cylindrical cloud with a uniform density, incorporating ambipolar diffusion, and subsequently analyze the resulting growth rates of unstable modes. Our findings indicate that ambipolar diffusion significantly influences the instability of these clouds, particularly in the low-density regime. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the instability growth rate is notably higher when ambipolar diffusion is included compared to scenarios where it is neglected.

We examine the quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno phenomena within a two-level system strongly coupled to a bosonic bath. By employing a nonperturbative approach, we demonstrate that the system's decay rate can be either enhanced or suppressed through frequent projective measurements.

This study examines the thermal coherence of the Heisenberg model incorporating Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya (DM) interactions within an inhomogeneous external field. We derive the analytical expressions for the reduced density matrix and the corresponding coherence measure. Our results indicate that the DM interaction significantly influences the coherence of the system. Furthermore, we analyze how the coherence varies with temperature and the strength of the DM interaction.

This study introduces a distributed trajectory planning approach for quadrotor swarms that ensures collision avoidance and maintains feasibility. The method employs a linear safe corridor (LSC) to define a collision-free region for each agent, with the corridor's width dynamically adjusted based on the agent's velocity. To ensure the algorithm remains feasible, the authors propose a distributed model predictive control (MPC) framework that incorporates the LSC as a constraint. The resulting MPC problem is formulated as a second-order cone program (SOCP), which is solved in real-time using a distributed algorithm. The study demonstrates the method's effectiveness through simulations involving a swarm of quadrotors.

This paper introduces CARLANE, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) methods for lane detection. CARLANE comprises 10,000 images from five distinct domains: one simulated environment and four real-world scenarios. The dataset is constructed to address the domain gap between synthetic and real data, as well as the variations among different real-world conditions. To support the benchmark, we provide baseline results using the state-of-the-art UDA method, UDA-Net, and release the code for reproducibility. The dataset and associated resources are accessible at https://github.com/zhengyuan1996/CARLANE.

The study examines how the receding contact angle of water droplets on hydrogels changes with the inclusion of particles. It demonstrates that the receding angle can be adjusted by varying the particle concentration, with the underlying mechanism attributed to the particles' influence on the hydrogel's surface energy.

This study examines the relationship between student connectivity and academic performance during the COVID-19 pandemic. Utilizing data from a large-scale, online, introductory statistics course at a major U.S. university, we analyzed the interactions of 1,000 students across 15 weeks of instruction. Our findings indicate that students with higher connectivity scores achieved better grades, a correlation that remained consistent regardless of the specific instructional method employed. Additionally, we observed that connectivity scores were positively linked to the frequency of student participation in class discussions.

This study introduces a new method for rapidly profiling wind speed at varying altitudes using Doppler radar. The technique relies on the assumption that wind speed remains constant over short distances, allowing the system to estimate the wind speed at a specific range by averaging measurements from neighboring ranges. This approach is implemented using the L-band Doppler radar at the University of Oklahoma, which is part of the NEXRAD network. The system's performance was evaluated by comparing its wind speed estimates against those derived from the traditional Doppler velocity spectrum method. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves a root-mean-square error of 0.6 m/s, representing a 30% improvement over the standard technique.

We present a comprehensive study of the open cluster UBC 274, utilizing data from the Gaia mission, the VLT/FLAMES survey, and the VLT/FLAMES survey. Our analysis reveals that the cluster is spatially and kinematically fragmented, with a total mass of approximately $1.5 \times 10^4 M_{\odot}$ and a mean age of 100 Myr. The cluster's core is characterized by a high density of young, massive stars, while its outskirts contain a significant population of older, low-mass stars. This structural dichotomy suggests that UBC 274 is currently undergoing tidal disruption. This study examines the impact of synthetic translations on bitext quality. We introduce a new metric, the Synthetic Translation Quality (STQ) score, designed to evaluate bitext quality by comparing it against synthetic translations. Our findings indicate that the STQ score correlates with the quality of machine translation systems, suggesting that it can effectively assess bitext quality.

We investigate the entanglement dynamics of a spin-1/2 XXZ chain coupled to a dissipative environment, where the Lindblad operators are engineered to be non-local. By analyzing the time evolution of the entanglement entropy, we identify a transition between logarithmic growth and an area law. This transition is governed by the competition between the dissipation rate and the system's intrinsic couplings.

We examine the spin-orbit coupling within the flat bands of transition metal dichalcogenide heterobilayers, specifically focusing on the MoTe$_2$/WSe$_2$ system. Our findings indicate that the spin-orbit coupling in these flat bands is significantly stronger than in the corresponding monolayers. This enhancement is attributed to the interplay between the spin-orbit coupling of the constituent monolayers and the interlayer hopping, which is driven by the distinct crystal symmetries of the two materials.

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is a machine learning framework that leverages the inherent complexity of quantum systems to process information. This study introduces a QRC architecture designed for finite-dimensional quantum systems, specifically utilizing a single qubit. We demonstrate that this system can effectively learn and forecast time series data, including chaotic sequences. Furthermore, we examine the impact of varying the reservoir's internal parameters on the system's performance.

We introduce a novel approach for atomically stable trapping using a GaN-on-Sapphire chip, which offers a superior alternative to traditional glass or silicon substrates. This method involves depositing a thin layer of Gallium Nitride onto a Sapphire substrate, followed by the application of a metallic coating to create a stable trap. The study details the fabrication process, evaluates the material's optical and mechanical characteristics, and outlines the experimental setup required for atom trapping.

This study examines the performance of the MFEM library for solving the Poisson equation using both Lagrange and Mixed finite element methods. The research evaluates the accuracy of these approaches by comparing their respective error norms.

This study examines a class of interacting dark energy models characterized by a sign-changing interaction term, $Q = \pm 3H\left(\frac{\rho_{\rm DE}}{1+z}\right)^n$, where $H$ denotes the Hubble parameter, $\rho_{\rm DE}$ represents dark energy density, $z$ is the redshift, and $n$ is a constant. The analysis explores the dynamical behavior of the system, revealing that the interaction term's sign determines the nature of the fixed points. Specifically, the system exhibits a stable saddle point when the interaction is negative, whereas it displays a stable spiral point when the interaction is positive. Furthermore, the study investigates the system's statefinder parameters, $r$ and $s$, to evaluate its cosmological evolution.

We examine the acceleration of particles at quasi-perpendicular shocks within the jets of tidal disruption events (TDEs) by employing a hybrid-particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. Our results indicate that the shock's quasi-perpendicularity significantly influences the acceleration efficiency. Specifically, the ratio of the shock's obliquity angle to the particle's pitch angle is a critical factor; when this ratio is small, the acceleration efficiency is notably reduced. Furthermore, we observe that the spectral index of the accelerated particles is highly sensitive to the shock's obliquity angle.

This study examines the acoustic cavitation of micro-bubbles within a resonant state, utilizing a time-domain framework. The analysis employs the Keller-Miksis equation to model bubble dynamics, incorporating the Rayleigh-Plesset equation alongside the Gilmore equation. The findings indicate that the bubble's resonant frequency is contingent upon its initial radius, the surrounding medium's density, and the speed of sound. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the bubble's resonant frequency is independent of the driving acoustic pressure.

Detecting stress is a critical challenge in healthcare, particularly for identifying individuals at risk of developing mental health disorders. While existing methods often rely on unimodal data, such as solely facial expressions or speech, they frequently fail to capture the full complexity of human behavior. This paper introduces MUSER, a novel multimodal framework designed to detect stress by integrating facial, speech, and physiological signals. The system employs a multi-task learning strategy, where stress detection is the primary objective and emotion recognition serves as an auxiliary task. This approach leverages the strong correlation between stress and emotional states to enhance the model's performance. Experimental results demonstrate that MUSER surpasses current state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 10% improvement in stress detection accuracy.

PanGEA is a toolkit designed for annotating panoramic graphs, which are directed graphs where nodes represent images and edges signify the spatial relationships between them. This tool supports various annotation tasks, including labeling images with semantic tags, defining edge weights, and creating new panoramic graphs from existing ones. It is built on the Python programming language and utilizes the NetworkX library for graph management. PanGEA offers a user-friendly interface that allows for the creation of panoramic graphs through multiple methods, such as importing from existing graphs, uploading image files, or generating them from scratch. Additionally, the toolkit provides a suite of functions for analyzing panoramic graphs, such as calculating the shortest path between two nodes, determining the total number of nodes, and identifying the most frequently occurring semantic tags.

The "downsizing" phenomenon describes the trend where massive galaxies cease star formation earlier than their low-mass counterparts. This study examines the impact of varying the initial mass function (IMF) and the rate of Type Ia supernovae (SNIa) on this trend. We utilize the semi-analytic model GALFORM to simulate galaxy evolution, incorporating a stellar IMF that varies with metallicity and a SNIa rate that depends on the star formation history. Our results indicate that while a metallicity-dependent IMF can alter the downsizing pattern, it does not eliminate it. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a SNIa rate linked to the star formation history can also modify the downsizing trend, though it does not remove it. We conclude that the downsizing phenomenon persists even when accounting for these variations in the IMF and SNIa rate.

This study introduces a novel image compressive sensing (CS) reconstruction framework that integrates group-based sparse representation with non-convex regularization. The proposed method first decomposes the input image into multiple groups, each characterized by a distinct dictionary, and then employs a non-convex regularization function to recover the sparse coefficients. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed non-convex regularization function yields a superior sparsity-promoting effect compared to conventional convex alternatives. Furthermore, an efficient algorithm is developed to solve the associated optimization problem. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves higher reconstruction quality than existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Detecting skin issues in facial images is a critical task for dermatologists, yet it remains challenging due to the scarcity of labeled data and the need for high precision. This paper introduces RethNet, a novel object-by-object learning framework designed to address these challenges. RethNet operates in two stages: first, it employs a pre-trained object detector to identify skin issues, and second, it utilizes a specialized classifier to determine the specific type of each detected problem. This approach offers two key advantages: it significantly reduces the demand for labeled data by leveraging pre-trained models, and it enhances detection accuracy by isolating the classification of individual skin issues. Experimental results demonstrate that RethNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in detecting facial skin problems.

This paper examines the performance and complexity of sequential decoding for polar accumulation (PAC) codes. PAC codes are constructed by concatenating polar codes with an accumulator, offering a low-complexity alternative to conventional polar codes that achieves the capacity of binary-input memoryless channels. We demonstrate that the error probability of PAC codes under sequential decoding decays exponentially with block length, with the error exponent determined by the channel's Bhattacharyya parameter. Furthermore, we derive an upper bound on the computational complexity of the decoder, showing that it grows polynomially with block length.

Sequential recommendation systems are designed to forecast a user's next item of interest by analyzing their historical interaction patterns. However, these models often struggle with cold-start users who have limited interaction history, resulting in poor recommendation quality. To address this, we introduce a novel meta-learning framework that leverages knowledge from users with abundant history to enhance recommendations for those with sparse data. Our approach utilizes a transitional learning strategy to align the feature distributions of cold-start and warm users, thereby enabling the sequential recommender to effectively transfer insights from well-established users to those with few interactions. Empirical evaluations on two real-world datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.
This paper provides a concise review of the current state of research into ultra-high energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), covering their origins, propagation, and detection.

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission aims to alter the orbit of the asteroid Dimorphos by impacting it with a spacecraft. This study examines how the projectile's shape influences the momentum transfer during such a collision. We conducted numerical simulations of impacts on a porous asteroid using the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method, varying the projectile's geometry. Our results indicate that the momentum transfer coefficient is significantly affected by the projectile's shape, with the most efficient impactors being those that are blunt and have a high aspect ratio. These findings are crucial for the DART mission, as they suggest that the spacecraft's current design may not be optimal for maximizing momentum transfer.

This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture designed to identify drivers through vehicle windshields. The system utilizes a high dynamic range (HDR) fusion approach that integrates both near-infrared (NIR) and visible light (VIS) images. The NIR modality is particularly effective for capturing facial details in low-light conditions, whereas the VIS modality excels in bright environments. By combining these complementary data sources, the model achieves superior performance in varying lighting scenarios. The architecture employs a dual-stream design, where each modality is processed by a dedicated convolutional neural network (CNN) branch. These branches are subsequently merged via a 3D convolutional layer to generate a unified feature representation. The model was evaluated on the THWDR dataset, which contains 1,000 images of 100 individuals captured under diverse lighting conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MU-Net surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy.

The Comprehensive Blub Archive Network (CBAN) is a proposed decentralized, distributed system designed to host open-source programming language repositories. This architecture aims to address the growing challenges of managing and accessing code, including the need for efficient search, version control, and collaboration. By leveraging blockchain technology, CBAN ensures data integrity, transparency, and immutability, while also providing a scalable and resilient infrastructure for the global developer community.

This study addresses the challenge of estimating the mean of a target variable when data are missing, specifically focusing on scenarios where covariates are also partially unobserved. We introduce a novel multistage estimation framework that integrates multiple imputation with propensity score weighting. This approach offers distinct advantages over existing methods, including the ability to handle missingness in both the outcome and covariates, the capacity to incorporate auxiliary information, and the flexibility to utilize various imputation models. We establish the asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator and derive its variance, which is then estimated using a robust sandwich formula. Simulation studies demonstrate that the method performs competitively against current state-of-the-art techniques. Finally, the approach is applied to analyze the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the stock market.
This paper examines a conjecture regarding the approximation of the complete elliptic integral of the first kind using the inverse hyperbolic tangent function.

Inductive procedure learning (IPL) involves deriving a program from input-output examples. This paper introduces a novel approach to IPL that decomposes the learning task into two distinct phases: first, identifying the program's structure, and second, determining its specific content. The proposed method utilizes a novel structural decomposition technique that breaks down a program into a set of sub-programs, each responsible for a single operation. This strategy is particularly effective for programs with high nesting levels, as it significantly reduces the search space. The study demonstrates the method's efficacy through experiments on various benchmarks, showing that it achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art techniques.

The proliferation of social media has significantly accelerated the spread of misinformation and fake news, which can cause severe societal harm. This study introduces a novel approach to automatically generate Arabic fake news by leveraging a pre-trained language model and a large-scale dataset of verified real news. We evaluate the generated content using both human assessments and automated metrics, demonstrating that the output is highly convincing and difficult to distinguish from authentic articles. Furthermore, we propose a detection framework based on a pre-trained language model to identify fabricated news. Experimental results indicate that the system achieves an F1-score of 0.91, confirming its effectiveness in distinguishing real news from the generated fakes.

This note provides a correction to the paper "Torsion subgroups of rational elliptic curves over the compositum of all $D_4$ extensions of the rational numbers" by the author, which appeared in the Journal of Number Theory, Volume 225, pages 1–10, in 2021.

We introduce a novel method for simulating multiqubit systems by employing matrix product operators (MPOs). This approach enables the investigation of nonlocal correlations within noisy quantum systems, specifically utilizing the quantum discord and entanglement of formation. Our findings indicate that entanglement of formation is highly sensitive to noise, whereas quantum discord remains robust against it. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the MPO technique is effective for modeling multiqubit systems with up to 10 qubits.

The objective is to maximize the diversity of the collected dataset by employing a tree-based approach that evaluates the diversity of candidate pages at each node.
